title: Solar System Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the 8 planets, dwarf planets, moons, rings, and asteroids orbiting our Sun.
seoTitle: Solar System Quiz – Planets, Moons & Asteroids | AI Quiz Arena
seoDescription: How well do you know our cosmic neighborhood? 10 fun questions on Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Venus, and planetary moons.

questions.question: Which planet is famously known as the 'Red Planet' due to iron oxide on its surface?
questions.explanation: Mars appears reddish because rust-like iron minerals in its soil and atmosphere oxidize under planetary conditions.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system by both diameter and mass?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet; it contains more than twice the combined mass of all other planets in the solar system.

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system has the hottest average surface temperature due to an extreme greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Venus has a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that traps heat, creating surface temperatures exceeding 460°C (860°F).

questions.question: Which gas giant is famous for having the most prominent and visible ring system?
questions.explanation: Saturn's spectacular rings are made primarily of countless chunks of water ice and rocky debris.

questions.question: What is the name of Jupiter's largest moon, which is also the largest moon in the entire solar system?
questions.explanation: Ganymede is larger in diameter than both Mercury and Pluto and possesses its own magnetic field.

questions.question: In what year was Pluto reclassified from a major planet to a 'dwarf planet' by the International Astronomical Union?
questions.explanation: In August 2006, the IAU established three criteria for full planets; Pluto failed to 'clear the neighborhood around its orbit'.

questions.question: Between which two planets is the main Asteroid Belt located?
questions.explanation: The main asteroid belt lies in the vast orbital expanse separating the inner terrestrial planet Mars and the outer gas giant Jupiter.

questions.question: What is the closest planet to the Sun?
questions.explanation: Mercury orbits closest to the Sun at an average distance of approximately 57.9 million kilometers (36 million miles).

questions.question: Which planet rotates on its side with an axial tilt of nearly 98 degrees?
questions.explanation: Uranus has an unusual 97.77-degree tilt, rotating almost parallel to its orbital plane, likely due to an ancient massive collision.

questions.question: What is the name of Saturn's largest moon, which has a dense atmosphere and liquid hydrocarbon lakes?
questions.explanation: Titan is the only moon known to have a dense atmosphere and stable surface liquid bodies (methane and ethane lakes).
